headline: High-risk filesystem and network overlap: Plandex can write shared project files while AutoGPT can execute shell and egress, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, and Plandex writes to a project directory with staged changes. That shared file bridge lets attacker-controlled content in Plandex outputs influence AutoGPT in default workflows. The interaction is documented only at profile level, so uncertainty does not reduce severity.
conditions: IF Plandex writes instructions or prompts into the shared project directory
IF AutoGPT ingests those files as trusted task context without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files
Require manual review of any file passed from Plandex to AutoGPT
Add provenance labels to shared artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce read-only handoff paths

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex reads and writes a project directory and sends context to a model provider; AutoGPT has filesystem access and network egress. If sensitive files are placed in the shared workspace, both agents can expose them through their respective inference or API paths. The profiles do not show data-class restrictions, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF sensitive files are stored in the shared project directory
IF either agent forwards file contents to an external model or API
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace
Use separate service accounts and API keys
Restrict outbound domains for both agents
Mount the project directory read-only for one agent
requires-engineering: add content-class filtering before upload

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and execute shell commands, while Plandex also modifies git state and supports multiple instances via shared backend state. In a shared repo, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide by default, risking lost work or corrupted state. This matches the high-risk overlap rubric more closely than medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or working tree
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while AutoGPT is also mutating files or git state
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Serialize git writes with a lock
Assign one agent read-only access
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex uses a review-then-apply workflow, but AutoGPT can still generate outputs that Plandex may treat as task input or plan material. If AutoGPT produces incorrect facts or commands, Plandex can propagate them into staged changes. The review step reduces but does not eliminate the cascade, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF AutoGPT outputs are copied into Plandex plans or prompts
IF Plandex applies changes without independent verification of AutoGPT claims
mitigations: Require human review before apply
Add a verification checklist for AutoGPT-derived claims
Keep AutoGPT outputs out of commit messages and patches
Use a second validator agent for critical changes
requires-engineering: add citation-backed claim checking

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. AutoGPT is open-source and Plandex is open-source with cloud or self-hosted options, so a compliance breach is not established from the profiles alone. The only concrete issue is that Plandex handles model-provider API keys, which is not itself a residency violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through a non-compliant deployment of Plandex
IF the operator uses a cloud backend without required contractual controls
mitigations: Deploy Plandex self-hosted for regulated data
Keep regulated data out of both agents
Review retention settings before use
Document the data flow for each workspace
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
